Fresno State - Cal‑PLASMA
DispatchPlasma science for chips, fusion, medicine, water and the workforce

News from the NSF-funded Cal-PLASMA Initiative led by Fresno State, and Cal Poly Pomona, plus the biggest plasma developments across industry and the jobs they're creating for our students.

A note from the PI

Welcome to the first Cal-PLASMA Dispatch. Every two weeks we'll gather what matters in plasma engineering, from the etch and deposition tools inside today's fabs to fusion machines, plasma therapies and plasma water treatment, and connect it to the work our students are doing.

This summer's first annual symposium showed how much energy there is across the campuses and our industry partners. This newsletter keeps that momentum going between meetings. Every issue includes a jobs board: the U.S. is building fabs and fusion plants faster than it's training people to run them, and our graduates should be first in lien to apply for these positions.

Sankha Banerjee, Ph.D., Professor of Mechanical Engineering, Fresno State, and PI, NSF ExLENT PLASMA (Award #2525980)

Fabs and plasma processing

Roughly half the steps in a modern chip flow touch a plasma: etch, PECVD and ALD, chamber cleaning and exhaust abatement. Here's what moved across equipment makers and fabs.

June 15 and June 25, 2026

Applied Materials rolls out new selective etch and plasma deposition tools for 3D chips

Applied, a Cal-PLASMA industry partner, introduced a Centris Spectral silicon nitride ALD system and a Producer Selectra molybdenum etch for wordline separation in 3D NAND, followed ten days later by a packaging suite that includes the Producer Avila 2 PECVD system for depositing stress-balanced films around through-silicon vias in HBM stacks.

Why it matters for students: selective etch, ALD and PECVD are exactly the processes behind the process-engineer openings in our jobs board below.

3D scaling announcement and DRAM and packaging release

September 30, 2026

TSMC weighs a second U.S. hub in Texas

TSMC is reportedly evaluating a Texas site that could host up to six advanced fabs, in addition to its Arizona cluster of 12 fabs, advanced packaging, and an R&D center.

DigiTimes

Q3 2026

Tools move into TSMC Arizona's second fab

Fab 21 Phase 2 finished construction early in 2026, equipment move-in has been underway this quarter, and high-volume 3 nm output is now targeted for 2027. Tool install means a hiring wave for equipment and process engineers in Phoenix.

Tech Insider

SK hynix breaks ground on its Indiana HBM plant

The groundbreaking marks the shift from funding announcements to physical construction of U.S.-based AI memory manufacturing, though output isn't expected until around 2028.

June 2026

Atomic layer etch goes into GaN production

Oxford Instruments says its plasma atomic-layer etch technology is supporting ROHM's in-house 200 mm gallium nitride manufacturing, a sign that ALE is moving from research tools to power-device lines.

Semiconductor Insight

September 30, 2026

Plasma abatement is the fastest-growing exhaust technology

A new market forecast expects plasma abatement to outpace thermal systems as fabs look for more efficient destruction of fluorinated gases from etch, deposition and chamber cleans.

Wafer-scale MoS₂ transistors with sub-5 nm channels

A CMU, University of Florida and MIT team reported wafer-scale monolayer MoS₂ transistors, part of a steady stream of 2D-material work aimed at scaling beyond silicon.

Semiconductor Engineering, Week in Review

Fusion

Private fusion is moving from physics experiments to construction schedules, supply contracts and licensing, and the timelines are getting real scrutiny.

September 2026

Helion closes a $500M round, opens a Seattle office, and resets its Orion timeline

Helion's Polaris prototype became the first private machine to show measurable deuterium-tritium fusion, reaching a 150 million °C plasma earlier this year. In September, the company closed an oversubscribed $500M Series G, said headcount has grown to about 800, and now expects to start up its Orion plant for Microsoft in 2028 with full power in 2029 or 2030.

Axios reported that Helion has softened earlier Polaris goals from net electricity to demonstrating electricity from fusion, and that two academic papers have questioned the energy-recovery assumptions behind its pulsed approach. Helion has published rebuttals.

Discussion prompt for our seminar: what would a credible, independently verifiable "electricity from fusion" milestone look like?

ANS Nuclear Newswire, The Fusion Report, Axios, World Nuclear Association

September 2026

SPARC nears completion and locks in its superconductor supply

Commonwealth Fusion Systems reports SPARC is close to 80% complete, its cryogenic system reached 8 K in mid-September, and on September 30 it agreed to buy more than 10,000 km of HTS tape from Fujikura. Operations are targeted for 2027.

Workforce snapshot

Fusion's workforce has quadrupled since 2021

The Fusion Industry Association counted about 4,600 direct private-fusion jobs in 2025 plus at least 9,300 in the supply chain. The most common openings are mechanical, electrical and power-electronics engineers, the core of our ME and EE programs.

Rejobs summary of FIA data

Plasma medicine

Cold atmospheric plasma delivers reactive oxygen and nitrogen species at body temperature. The 2026 literature is shifting from "does it work" to dose, depth and device design.

Published September 4, 2026

A roadmap for plasma in chronic disease

A Nano Research review maps plasma sources, reactive-species delivery routes and therapeutic mechanisms, and lays out the open questions that stand between lab results and routine clinical use.

Nano Research

2026

How deep does cold plasma actually reach?

A Frontiers review compiles penetration-depth data for CAP in biological tissue across antitumor, antimicrobial, wound-healing and transdermal drug-delivery uses. Useful reading for anyone designing a treatment protocol.

Frontiers in Bioengineering and Biotechnology

August 2026

Mechanisms behind plasma wound healing

A new review in IJMS works through the antimicrobial and regenerative mechanisms of CAP and its use on venous leg ulcers and other chronic wounds.

International Journal of Molecular Sciences

July 2026

Plasma versus MRSA biofilms

A systematic review of in vitro studies finds cold plasma can sharply reduce MRSA biofilms, with gliding-arc jets reaching roughly 3.5 to 5.4 log reductions after a one-minute treatment depending on biofilm age.

BioMed Research International

Closer to home: Fresno State's plasma micro-discharge work on 3D-printed PLA scaffolds targets the same goal from the materials side, using plasma to tune surfaces so cells attach selectively.

Water treatment and Ag-Tech

For the Central Valley, plasma's most practical near-term payoffs may be destroying "forever chemicals" and turning air and water into on-farm nitrogen.

July 2026

Bubbles plus cold plasma break down PFOS in tap water

Researchers paired cold atmospheric plasma with gas dispersion so that bubbles carry PFAS up to the plasma-liquid interface, where reactive species attack them. The setup degraded both long- and short-chain PFAS and released fluoride as treatment continued, showing the C–F bonds were actually being broken. The team is now scaling the reactor to larger volumes.

Connection: This mirrors the plasma-liquid coupling questions in our micro-plasma and graphene membrane platform and in the CSU ARI irrigation water recycling project.

ScienceDaily summary and Scientific Reports paper

Market outlook, 2026 to 2035

Plasma-activated water for fertilizer is leaving the pilot stage

Global Market Insights sizes the plasma-activated water fertilizer market at about $35M in 2026 and projects strong growth through 2035, led by controlled-environment agriculture and on-site plasma nitrogen units now in commercial operation. Capital cost remains the barrier for small and mid-size growers.

Global Market Insights

Research

Plasma-treated wastewater boosts melon seedlings

Work in the Journal of Physics D found that plasma-activated wastewater improved germination and seedling growth of Cucumis melo by up to 130% over controls, pointing to a combined fertilization and water-reuse pathway.

Masaryk University publication record

Research

Ceramic-coated electrodes for longer-lived PFAS reactors

A dielectric barrier discharge reactor with a plasma-sprayed Cr₂O₃ electrode coating resisted corrosion while also concentrating PFOA near the plasma-liquid film, improving removal.

Chemical Engineering Science

Bachelor's path

Field service, equipment and manufacturing engineering are the fastest way into a fab. New tool installs in Arizona and Texas are driving demand right now.

Master's path

Process and product engineering roles at equipment makers increasingly want hands-on etch or deposition hours. Thesis work in plasma processing counts.

Build your edge

List the specific tools and techniques you've used (PECVD, sputtering, XRD, FTIR, SEM) on your résumé. Recruiters search for them by name.
